transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2028-06-30
- Start: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 46 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Iris (Redwood Product), Ellen (Deckline Head of MLOps), Jonah (Deckline SRE), Priya (Deckline Product), Marco (Deckline Finance)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Deckline is evaluating Redwood Console to get per-route breakdowns of inference usage and to diagnose an unexpected spike in costs. We walked through the Console: per-route dashboards, top-consuming routes, token-level cost attribution, and Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization). Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted (burst capacity, SLAs) and private deployment concerns (KMS, VPC). Action: share pricing, run POC benchmark, send SOC2 docs.

Topics covered:
- Console per-route dashboards and filters
- Token and request-level cost attribution
- Optimize recommendations (batching, cache, quantization)
- Dedicated capacity and burst policy implications
- Security: KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
- POC benchmark plan and success criteria

Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect in places):
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can do a quick intro and then jump into the Console demo. Uh Samir and I will take the walkthrough, Iris is on for product questions.
[00:12] Ellen: Hi, thanks. Quick context — last month our inference bill spiked about 42% and finance is, uh, not happy. We're trying to understand which endpoints / routes drove that. Also we have a strict timeline for a pilot in Q3.
[00:28] Samir: Got it. That's exactly the sort of thing the per-route lenses in the Console were built for — you can map requests to logical routes, see token breakdowns, and then trace back to the model variant and runtime.
[00:38] Jonah: One thing, we often see noisy long-halts on certain latency-sensitive routes, and sometimes the KV cash gets warm/cold and it changes cost — apologies, that's KV cache.
[00:52] Maya: No worries. We'll show both the telemetry and the cost decomposition so you can correlate the latency spikes with token counts and batching inefficiencies.
[01:05] Samir: Sharing screen — starting on the Console home, quick glance at usage heatmap. You can change time ranges, group by route, model, or region. I'll filter to Deckline production for the last 30 days.
[01:25] Samir: Okay we can see a top-10 routes list; route " /summarize-doc" is heavy. Click into the route dashboard — on the left is throughput and latency timeline, middle is token distribution per request, right is cost attribution by token type (prompt vs completion).
[01:45] Priya: The cost attribution graph — is that accurate down to the token? We need to tie invoices to product feature owners.
[01:54] Iris: Yes, we compute per-token compute units based on model profile and runtime variant. There's a mapping so finance can export CSVs for chargeback to feature teams.
[02:12] Marco: Is there an export for our billing tool? We use an internal ledger and want the per-route CSV.
[02:20] Samir: Yep, export to CSV is built-in and there's an API endpoint to pull route-level spend, you can backfill if needed.
[02:29] Ellen: Show the period where the spike happened — end of May.
[02:34] Samir: Narrowing to May 24–28. Ah — see this surge here, but it's only on one variant, the 'r2-small-q4' quantized variant. There's also a corresponding increase in average request length — looks like upstream changed prompts.
[02:58] Jonah: Wait, upstream changed prompts — that makes sense, we shipped a change to include full chat history in the prompt by mistake.
[03:07] Maya: That explains the token bump. In the Console you can also view 'prompt templates' associated with routes so you can trace to commit or owner.
[03:20] Samir: Another item: batching efficiency. For that route the batching window is set to 5ms which is low; increasing to 20–30ms in Dedicated can improve throughput and lower per-token cost but may add latency tail.
[03:36] Ellen: Latency is sensitive for that route — under 250ms p95 is our SLO.
[03:42] Samir: Understood. We can show the tradeoff with the Optimize recommendations. Switching to the Optimize tab — here's automatic suggestions: increase batching window to 25ms for batchable requests, enable prefix KV caching for the common intro text, and try a 4-bit quantized model for cheaper durable workloads.
[04:05] Priya: The KV cache suggestion — does that require code changes?
[04:10] Samir: Minimal — it's an API flag and a small client library update to identify prefix tokens. We can share the runbook.
[04:18] Jonah: On Dedicated — what's the burst policy? We need predictable throughput during peak traffic but still want cost controls.
[04:27] Maya: Dedicated supports a reserved pool and burst buckets; you can set autoscale thresholds and a hard cap. We can show pricing scenarios vs hosted.
[04:36] Marco: Which one is cheaper for spiky traffic, Dedicated or hosted with bursts?
[04:42] Iris: It depends — steady high throughput favors Dedicated commit discounts; spiky but moderate overall usage sometimes is cheaper on hosted with burst credits. Samir, you have a quick calc?
[04:54] Samir: I pulled a sample: if 70% of traffic is steady and 30% is bursts, Dedicated with 20% overprovision and burst buffer ended up 18% cheaper in our model. But if bursts are short and infrequent, hosted wins due to zero commit. We'll share a spreadsheet tailored to Deckline numbers.
[05:15] Ellen: About security — we need KMS integration for keys, SSO via SAML, and audit logs forwarded to Splunk.
[05:25] Maya: All supported. For Private we can deploy control plane in your VPC, integrate with your KMS/HSM, and forward audit streams. There's also RBAC at the token and route level in Console.
[05:40] Jonah: What's the expected effort for on-prem/private?
[05:45] Maya: Typical on-prem packaging takes 4–6 weeks for review and networking, depending on PoPs and airgapped needs. For VPC host it can be faster. We'll send the whitepaper.
[05:57] Priya: We also want an alert if cost exceeds budget for a route.
[06:02] Samir: Console supports alerts by route, model, or tag. You can set thresholds on daily spend or percent over baseline and tie to PagerDuty or Slack.
[06:12] Ellen: Walk me through a practical example: set an alert if /summarize-doc costs > $1,000/day.
[06:20] Samir: Sure — in Alerts you create a new rule, scope it to route /summarize-doc, metric 'route_cost', condition 'greater than', value 1000, then set notification channel. We also support auto-fallback policies — you can fallback to a cheaper variant when cost or latency breaches.
[06:40] Jonah: The auto-fallback — is it per-request or traffic-split?
[06:45] Samir: Both: you can do percentage rollouts or prefer cheaper variant for non-critical requests. There's also circuit-breaker style policies.
[06:55] Marco: Finance will want tokenized line items per feature team — can we tag routes and export grouped spend?
[07:02] Iris: Yes, route tags map to billing dimensions. Many customers map to product, environment, and owner tags.
[07:12] Ellen: You mentioned model profiling earlier. Can Console show per-model perf profiles?
[07:18] Samir: Yep — under Model Catalog each model has a profile: per-token cost, latency distribution by sequence length, preferred kernels. That helps choose quantization levels.
[07:30] Priya: If we try 4-bit quantization for a low-risk route, how do we measure quality drift?
[07:36] Iris: You can connect an eval suite to the Console — run prompt sets and regression alerts. We flag declines in rouge/accuracy metrics and tie to specific model variants.
[07:48] Maya: For the POC we recommend a three-step plan: sync on success criteria, run an isolated benchmark on DVD (Deckline test environment) for 100k requests with representative prompts, then a 2-week canary in production with route tags and cost/quality gates.
[08:05] Ellen: Success criteria — p95 latency under 250ms, cost per 1k tokens reduced by 10% without quality loss > 1% on our eval metric.
[08:18] Maya: Good, we'll document that in the POC runbook.
[08:23] Samir: Quick demo: creating a POC sandbox in Console — I'm creating a sandbox project, uploading model variant, and wiring a test route. You can replay traffic and compare cost before/after.
[08:40] (screen demo noise, occasional cross talk)
[08:52] Jonah: The replay — can we replay anonymized production traces?
[08:56] Samir: Yes, you can scrub PII and replay traces; we also support synthetic traffic generators.
[09:06] Priya: A small UI nit — can we pin dashboards for our leadership?
[09:10] Maya: Dashboards can be pinned and shared; you can also create read-only viewer roles and link dashboards to Slack.
[09:20] Marco: Any mentions of competitor integrations? We use some proprietary components and Anthropic for safety checks.
[09:27] Iris: We have model adapters; you can bring your own model or mix hosted models. Integrations are flexible.
[09:36] Ellen: For the POC, we'll need a checklist from Redwood on networking and sample IAM policies.
[09:42] Maya: We'll send a POC checklist and a template VPC peering doc.
[09:47] Jonah: Regarding the billing export, a couple of our engineers want an example API call to pull route-level spend.
[09:53] Samir: I'll attach a sample curl in the follow-up email.
[10:00] (longer silence as screen demo continues)
[10:20] Priya: Does the Console show cold-starts per model or container? We suspect a cold-start pattern early morning that drives latency spikes.
[10:28] Samir: Yes, cold-start heatmap is visible in infra metrics; you can see allocation events and correlate to p95 spikes. Also warm pools in Dedicated help reduce those cold-starts.
[10:42] Ellen: Can we set up a cost budget per route with auto-mitigation?
[10:47] Samir: Yes, set budget scope to route, configure mitigation to either throttle non-critical percent or fallback to cheaper variant. We'll demo automation in the POC.
[10:58] Maya: Quick questions from my side — do you have compliance constraints beyond SOC 2?
[11:03] Ellen: Mostly SOC 2 + internal pen tests; potential healthcare data in future.
[11:08] Maya: We'll include HIPAA considerations in the whitepaper, though private on-prem would be recommended for PHI.
[11:16] Jonah: Anything else on hardware selection? We run on GCP with A2 family — curious how Redwood maps kernels.
[11:23] Samir: The runtime includes a kernel selector that chooses optimal ops for A2/TPU/RTX. We surface recommended GPU families per model in the Model Catalog.
[11:35] Priya: Ok, let's recap next steps — who will do what.
[11:40] Maya: I'll email pricing and SLA options, plus SOC2 and POC checklist. Samir will prepare the POC runbook, sample curl, and the benchmark script. Ellen will gather internal availability and sample prompt sets for the 100k test.
[11:54] Ellen: Sounds good. Marco will sign off on budget once we get the pricing spreadsheet.
[12:02] Maya: Great thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Wednesday with the materials and proposed POC dates.

End of meeting.

Notes about transcription quality: occasional word swaps (KV cash / KV cache), imperfect proper nouns. The transcript preserves natural speech patterns and interruptions.
